issues.location: GNU Make section (Targets, Prerequisites & Recipes through Phony Targets)
issues.issue: The entire GNU Make section — targets, prerequisites, recipes, timestamp evaluation, self-updating builds, dependency tree resolution, intermediate object files, make variables, clean targets, .PHONY — is completely absent from the source material. The source is the MIT Missing Semester Shell lecture, which contains zero Make content. This appears to be from a different lesson and must be removed from this wiki page.

issues.location: File Permissions (ls -l), Wildcards & Globs, Bash Quoting, Shell Built-ins vs External Programs (child process memory isolation), Background Jobs (detailed), Parameter Expansion sections
issues.issue: These sections expand well beyond the lecture content (drawing from exercises or external knowledge) but present the material as if it were part of the lecture, with no source-scope disclaimer. The awk section correctly includes one ('Source scope: the lecture teaches only {print $2} and -F,'), but these sections do not. A student reading them would not know what came from the lecture versus what was added by the implementer. Each expanded section needs a scope note similar to the awk section's.
